trust_decision.summary: Whether the request Origin header is trusted enough to be reflected in Access-Control-Allow-Origin (with Allow-Credentials: true) is decided in ApiApplication::respond and ::handlePreflight; at the pinned commit respond() reflects any Origin unconditionally and the preflight ignores the request Origin entirely.

landing_point.why: The only place in the tree that reflects HTTP_ORIGIN into Access-Control-Allow-Origin; a grep for 'Access-Control' or 'cors_allow_origin' lands here immediately.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any /api/index.php/v1/* request with CORS enabled (ApiApplication::respond, every non-OPTIONS response)
HTTP OPTIONS preflight on any /api/index.php/v1/* route with CORS enabled (ApiApplication::route -> handlePreflight)
Admin Global Configuration save (com_config application.save) - default value of cors_allow_headers only, functional not a check
Installer configuration writer - default cors_allow_headers only
Global Configuration form default for cors_allow_headers

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both checking sites are in libraries/src/Application/ApiApplication.php (respond at :165-190, handlePreflight at :308-359); the other CORS-related changes only alter the cors_allow_headers default (administrator/components/com_config/src/Model/ApplicationModel.php:744, installation/src/Model/ConfigurationModel.php:410), not the origin check.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The setting's own description says the origin is 'sent back in response to a preflight request' (administrator/language/en-GB/com_config.ini:214), so a solver could fix handlePreflight only and argue the respond() path for actual responses is outside the setting's documented scope; it sits in the same file 130 lines apart, so the lever is weak.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Wildcard config '*' (the shipped default) must keep returning Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * without credentials, and a configured allowed origin must still get a 204 preflight with Allow-Headers/Allow-Methods; an over-broad fix (drop CORS entirely, 403 every preflight, or reject multi-origin lists) breaks API clients.

O6_input_shapes: configured comma-separated list of origins with surrounding whitespace (trim + explode)
request Origin not in the whitelist (preflight -> 403, actual response -> no ACAO header)
Origin read raw rather than via the 'string' filter (pinned code uses getString at libraries/src/Application/ApiApplication.php:182-183)

O7_producer.where: cors_allow_origin is produced by the Global Configuration save path administrator/components/com_config/src/Model/ApplicationModel.php:743 (form field administrator/components/com_config/forms/application.xml:344-352, dist default installation/configuration.php-dist:123) and read via $this->get() at libraries/src/Application/ApiApplication.php:178 and :336

O8b_injection_room.sibling: API error responses call sendHeaders() directly and bypass ApiApplication::respond; a copy that adds CORS headers here (so browser clients can read API errors) would need the same origin check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Cross-origin API clients cannot read error bodies without ACAO, so a maintainer adding CORS to the error path is a plausible feature request; it is a different file/package (Exception vs Application).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The 409/404 early exits send headers and close() without respond(); a planted CORS header block here would be a second implementation in the MVC layer.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same motivation as above: early-exit JSON responses lose CORS headers, and the natural patch copies the respond() block.

O9_family: CORS origin validation / reflected-origin trust (advisory labels CWE-93 but the mechanism is origin reflection with credentials, not CRLF)

services: none required for a unit test of ApiApplication; full API install needs a database (MySQL/PostgreSQL)
O10_build.project_tests: No existing unit or integration tests reference ApiApplication or CORS under tests/ at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Compare HTTP_ORIGIN against cors_allow_origin in respond() only, as a single exact string (no comma list, no wildcard handling), leaving handlePreflight unchanged.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commits are whole release bundles (5.4.8 / 6.1.3) carrying roughly ten unrelated security fixes: batch-copy ACL (libraries/src/MVC/Model/AdminModel.php, com_categories/com_menus/com_modules/com_fields models), API core.manage checks (libraries/src/MVC/Controller/ApiController.php, api/components/*), MFA captive task allow-lists, SHTML forbidden extensions, schema.org JSON escaping and view levels, Content-Disposition quote stripping (com_banners RawView, com_contact VcfView). Only the ApiApplication changes belong to this advisory.
Content-Disposition filename quote stripping (fix.diff:14, fix.diff:657) matches the header-injection hint but belongs to a different advisory; not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell used); Joomla CMS is well above the 5 MB tiny threshold and below 1.5 GB.
present_in_latest not applicable: O8 is empty and no latest release was provided.
Advisory label CWE-93 vs actual mechanism (origin reflection) not reconciled against the published advisory text beyond the summary.

Biggest practical concern: the published diff is a release bundle, so the task diff must be hand-extracted to the ApiApplication hunks (fix.diff:806-925 / fix.diff:2033-2152); not listed in O12 because no defined flag covers it.
